conversation.speaker: dialogue
conversation.text:
Police: Is there anything you want to say about Xiyuan’s life in kindergarten?
Respondent: I’ve already said everything else on the phone.
Respondent: She still hasn’t been found? How could something like this happen in broad daylight? And inside the residential complex...
Respondent: I heard that at the time, Xiyuan’s mother and older brother were both there. Did they really not see anything?
Respondent: Xiyuan... I don’t know whether saying this will help you.
Respondent: Since you said I can say anything, then I’ll say it.
Respondent: Xiyuan has always had a lively and cheerful personality.
Respondent: When I first met her last year, she wasn’t shy at all. She even startled several of us teachers.
Respondent: At first, I thought she was just easygoing.
Respondent: Since her mom is gone, most of the time it was her older brother who came to pick her up, but I never saw her look for her mom.
Respondent: If you ask whether she had any problems... none at all. She had no problems whatsoever.
Respondent: It’s just...
Respondent: I never saw her cry, nor did I ever see her get angry or throw a tantrum... Do you understand what I mean?
Respondent: I often told myself that a child like her needs even more of my attention, and that I must take even more careful care of her.
Respondent: Because I always felt... her smile was like a bubble under the sunlight. It looks beautiful, but it would burst with just the slightest touch.
Respondent: Do you understand that feeling?
